circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi designed by Hermann Tilke, has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. The circuit represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One destination, following Bahrain and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street track that loops around Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Australian Grand Prix as its primary Formula One event along with supporting racing series. The circuit maintains FIA Grade 1 certification status.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit has a storied history of hosting the Austrian Grand Prix across two distinct eras, first as the Österreichring from 1970 to 1987, then following reconstruction and renaming as the A1-Ring from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street course in Azerbaijan's capital that spans 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest track currently used in Formula One. Following its debut as host of the 2016 European Grand Prix, the venue became home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards, with operations managed by the Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix that year. The track, holding an FIA Grade 1 license with multiple configurations, has accommodated various motorsport series including GP2 racing and 24-hour endurance events, along with Australian V8 Supercars between 2006 and 2010.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located near Barcelona in Montmeló, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit features a balanced mix of extended straightaways and diverse cornering sequences that test multiple aspects of driver and car performance. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The Belgian circuit near Spa stretches over 7 kilometers through the Walloon countryside and has served as the home of the Belgian Grand Prix since 1925, making it one of Formula One's oldest venues. The track has hosted races continuously from 1950 onwards, with only brief absences in 2003 and 2006, cementing its status as a regular fixture on the modern calendar.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve spans 4. 361 kilometres and serves as the permanent home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond hosting Formula One, the track has accommodated various international racing series including sports car championships, open-wheel competitions, and stock car events throughout its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit in Jiading has served as the primary venue for China's Formula One Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 through 2019 before resuming in 2024. Located in Shanghai, the facility has expanded its motorsport portfolio to include electric racing events alongside its traditional role as host of the Chinese Grand Prix.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone and Whittlebury in Northamptonshire, this English racing facility has hosted the British Grand Prix since 1948 and was the venue for the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After the British Grand Prix rotated among three circuits between 1955 and 1986, it became a permanent fixture at this track from 1987 onward, which also stages MotoGP events.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, a 4. 381 km circuit located near Budapest in Mogyoród, hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held behind the Iron Curtain in 1986. Built in just eight months starting from October 1985, faster than any other F1 venue, the track was constructed outside the city near a highway after initial plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park were rejected by authorities.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale di Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. The track hosts the Italian Grand Prix nearly every year since 1949, making it one of the few circuits to remain continuously on the Formula One schedule, and earns its "Temple of Speed" nickname from its notably long straightaways and fast-paced corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, a 5. 807 km track in Mie Prefecture, Japan, serves as a premier venue for international motorsport competition. Operated by Honda Mobilityland, the facility hosts Formula One and Super Formula races and accommodates approximately 155,000 spectators.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, running alongside the famous Las Vegas Strip on Las Vegas Boulevard. The 3. 8-kilometre track passes iconic casino resorts and entertainment venues, incorporating landmark structures such as the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas into its layout.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both accomplished racers who died in separate accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The track has served as the venue for Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix since 2015, reviving a motorsport tradition that previously took place there on an alternate configuration until 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, the track became home to the Miami Grand Prix starting in 2022, and has since been adapted for Formula E racing from the 2025–26 season onwards.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street course that winds through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine in the Principality of Monaco, surrounding the harbour area. Though officially named after the circuit itself, it is widely known as the Monte Carlo circuit due to its location primarily within that neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Nestled in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, the 4. 259 km Zandvoort circuit hosted the Netherlands' return to Formula One when it rejoined the calendar in 2021. The track's partnership with the sport concluded following the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit, situated north of Doha in Qatar, is a 5. 419 km track featuring a 1. 068 km main straight and holds an FIA Grade 1 license.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km circuit in São Paulo, Brazil, that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and features an associated kart facility honoring fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: A street circuit situated along Jeddah's waterfront promenade overlooking the Red Sea, this venue has hosted the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its introduction to the Formula One calendar in 2021. The facility also began hosting an international electric racing championship race in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a street-based racing venue located around Singapore's Marina Bay, incorporating urban zones from the Downtown Core and Kallang districts.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657 km motorsport venue features a balanced design combining extended straightaways with diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing multiple racing disciplines. The track holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 FIA facility that serves as the home venue for the Formula One United States Grand Prix. The track hosts multiple international racing series including MotoGP, NASCAR, and the FIA World Endurance Championship, alongside its previous tenure with various American and international motorsport competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver who represents Thailand in Formula One and currently drives for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has secured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 while accumulating 32 race victories over 23 seasons. Beyond the F1 grid, Alonso stands as the only driver to have won both the Formula One and World Endurance championships, with notable achievements including two Le Mans 24 Hours victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship title.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli made his Formula One debut in 2025 and currently races for Mercedes, having secured eight race victories in the championship.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British driver currently racing in Formula One with Haas. He has established himself as a professional motorsports competitor at the highest level of single-seater racing.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One racing for Audi, bringing his professional motorsport background to the sport's highest level.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after a lengthy career that includes two runner-up championship finishes with Mercedes in consecutive years. Across his 13 seasons in the sport, Bottas has accumulated 10 Grand Prix victories.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Argentine driver Franco Alejandro Colapinto currently races for Alpine in Formula One competition.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan balances his commitments as a reserve pilot for Haas in Formula One with an active racing programme in European Le Mans Series prototypes. He made seven Grand Prix appearances during the 2024-2025 season while competing in the LMP2 category for Nielsen Racing.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: French driver Pierre Gasly currently races for Alpine in Formula One, having previously achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Hadjar, a French-Algerian competitor, represents France on the Formula One grid while driving for Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding the joint-record of seven world championship titles alongside Michael Schumacher. He leads the sport in multiple statistical categories, including victories, pole positions, and podium finishes.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi, bringing extensive experience from his long career in the sport. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he achieved notable success in endurance racing, securing victory at the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 as part of the Porsche team.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand motorsport competitor, currently drives for Racing Bulls in the Formula One championship.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver, represents Ferrari in Formula One and has claimed nine race victories over his career. He finished second in the 2022 drivers' championship while driving for the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen returned to Formula One for a second stint between 2022 and 2024, following his initial career in the series from 2014 to 2020. Currently, he competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship with BMW and WRT, while also undertaking part-time NASCAR Cup Series commitments with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship title. Throughout his eight-season career in the sport, he has secured 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The driver achieved his sole Grand Prix victory in 2021 at the Hungarian Grand Prix while competing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez, a Mexican driver, competes in Formula One for Cadillac. The veteran racer finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while with Red Bull and has secured six race victories throughout his 15-year career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri competes for McLaren in Formula One, where he has secured nine Grand Prix victories over his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One from 2011 through 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his 14-season career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: The British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Carlos Sainz Jr. is a Spanish Formula One driver currently competing for Williams who has secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to international sports car racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category for Proton Competition, having previously driven LMP2 machinery for Era Motorsport in IMSA competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver who currently races for Aston Martin in the championship series.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese racing driver, holds a reserve position with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls after competing as a full-time Formula One driver from 2021 through 2025. He transitioned to a backup role beginning in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch driver Max Verstappen has achieved four consecutive world championship titles between 2021 and 2024 while competing for Red Bull Racing. Over his 12-season Formula One career, he has secured 73 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China as a racing driver currently holding a reserve position with Cadillac in Formula One. He competed in the sport's top category between 2022 and 2024, holding the distinction of being the sole Chinese driver to have participated in the championship.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team operated as Renault's official Formula One entry from its rebranding as Alpine in 2021 through the 2025 season, when the French manufacturer ended its direct involvement in the sport. Originally established under the Renault F1 Team name and backed by Groupe Renault, the operation was repositioned to highlight the Alpine sports car marque during its final five years of competition.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automobile manufacturer, has held multiple entries throughout Formula One history and currently competes as Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team under the AMR GP Limited operation.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker and stands as the sport's most enduring and accomplished outfit, participating in every Formula One World Championship since the series' inception in 1950. The team, colloquially identified by its prancing horse emblem, has established itself as an unparalleled force throughout the sport's history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas in 2014, this American-licensed outfit commenced Formula One racing in 2016 and has since become a competitive midfield presence in the championship. Leadership of the team transitioned in early 2024 when Ayao Komatsu assumed the principal role from Guenther Steiner, who had guided the squad since its inaugural campaign.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: This Swiss engineering and racing outfit, established in 1970, built sports cars before transitioning to Formula One machinery as an independent constructor. The team achieved significant endurance racing success, including overall victory at Le Mans in 1989, before competing in Formula One from 1993 until departing in 2025 as one of the sport's longest-serving constructors. Audi acquired the team and its operations in 2024 to establish the foundation for its own Formula One effort.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British racing outfit headquartered at its Technology Centre in Woking that competes in Formula One as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group. The team is owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: The Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, operating from Brackley under a German racing licence, represents Mercedes-Benz's current involvement in Formula One, a relationship spanning since 1954 as both constructor and engine supplier. From January 2022, ownership became equally shared among Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and Toto Wolff in a restructured partnership. The team carries the historical "Silver Arrows" designation associated with Mercedes' racing heritage.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the sport in 2024, operating as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team structure alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the team represents Red Bull's second constructor entry in the championship.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in the 2024 season as part of Red Bull's two-team structure. Based in Faenza with operations in Milton Keynes, the outfit operates as Red Bull's second racing entity alongside Red Bull Racing.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England and part of Red Bull GmbH's motorsport portfolio. Founded in 2005 and led by Christian Horner until his 2025 departure, the team has become one of the sport's major competitors, with Laurent Mekies taking over as team principal.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, which will compete as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in 2026, stands as a British Formula One constructor founded by Frank Williams and Patrick Head in 1977, succeeding Frank Williams's earlier failed racing venture. The team operates from its Grove, Oxfordshire headquarters on a substantial 60-acre facility.
